questions: Did the s-bend off-track count fall from 11 of 20 at y 0.07, and did its max_error drop below 0.048?
Did steering_oscillation stay below about 0.4 on the oval and s-bend, and did the oval finish stay near 1.0?
Did slalom line_loss_events fall below 1.0 (it was 1.0 at y 0.07)?
Is the controller still stable at y 0.08 with kp 4.0 and kd unchanged, or does the longer lookahead need a different kp or kd?
Did control_effort on the s-bend fall from 11.2, showing less steering effort per unit of error?

intent: Change one variable from the best design (iteration 4): move all sensors from y 0.07 to y 0.08, the top of the allowed range, keeping 16 mm footprints, the 0.024 m span, a 0.12 m track, 0.03 m wheels, the 0.12 m body and 0.8 kg mass. This tests whether the lookahead gain that rose from 0.06 to 0.07 continues to 0.08. Expected: s-bend off-track exits and max_error fall, oval finish near 1.0, and oscillation stays below 0.4.
learning: Iteration 4 showed that y 0.07 beats y 0.06 (534 vs 454.6, with oval finish 20/20 and s-bend finish 9/20). The lookahead trend is monotone so far. The Integrator's wheel_track 0.14 suggestion is doubtful, because turn rate per PWM difference falls as wheel_track rises; treat that as a test to run only if the lookahead gain stops.
rationale: Iteration 4 (y 0.07) is the best design so far at 534.0, up from 454.6 at y 0.06. Its oval finish rate is 20/20 with max_error 0.020 and oscillation 0.22, so the longer lookahead did not add jitter. Across the lookahead sweep the score runs 131.9 (y 0.04), 454.6 (y 0.06), 534.0 (y 0.07), a consistent gain from longer lookahead. The s-bend is still the main loss: 11 of 20 runs leave the track, max_error is 0.048, and control_effort is 11.2, so the robot is still late into bends. Slalom is 0/20 with line_loss 1.0, which is at the threshold for a change. Two options follow from the evidence. Integrator feedback (R1) proposes wheel_track 0.14, but I checked the physics and it is doubtful. Turn rate is the wheel speed difference divided by wheel_track, so a wider track gives less yaw per unit of PWM difference, which reduces steering authority rather than adding it. I am therefore not following that step yet. The monotone lookahead trend is the better-supported lever, and y 0.07 is still well inside the 0.08 limit. I will test y 0.08 as the single change, keeping 16 mm footprints, the 0.024 m span, wheel_track 0.12, kp 4.0 and kd as the Integrator set them. Expected result: s-bend off-track exits fall below about 9 of 20 and max_error drops below 0.048, oval finish stays near 1.0, and slalom line_loss stays near or below 1.0. Watch oscillation: if it rises above about 0.4 or the oval finish falls below 0.85, revert to y 0.07 and test a narrower track (wheel_track 0.10) or kp adjustment, since that gives more yaw per command.
